components.explanation: recorded manual: the record covering 84.5.0 describes the move from 84.4.0 to 84.5.0. Follow the steps below, then apply
components.summary: The upgrade deletes Grafana, Alertmanager, node-exporter, kube-state-metrics, the default rules and the dashboards. Prometheus stops loading PrometheusRules, Probes and ScrapeConfigs, keeps only the series AICR components query, and moves from its PVC to an emptyDir, so its history is lost.
components.precondition: Anything that reads this release's Grafana, Alertmanager or Prometheus history has another source, such as nktp.

steps.description: Export any Grafana dashboards, Alertmanager configuration, and PrometheusRules you still need.
Sync or reconcile the new bundle, upgrading this release before nktp.
steps.reason: nktp's node-exporter can't start while the old one holds host port 9100. The operator recreates Prometheus on an emptyDir, so prometheus-adapter's metrics are unavailable for about 30 seconds.

steps.description: Delete what the release leaves behind: kubectl delete pvc --ignore-not-found -n monitoring prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-db-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0; kubectl delete secret --ignore-not-found -n monitoring kube-prometheus-admission; kubectl delete service --ignore-not-found -n kube-system kube-prometheus-kubelet.
steps.reason: The deployer doesn't own them: the StatefulSet created the PVC, a hook Job created the Secret, and the operator created the Service.

components.explanation: recorded safe: the record covering 0.21.0 describes the move from v0.20.0 to v0.21.0, verified by "Chart diff v0.20.0 to v0.21.0: the CRDs change field descriptions and add one optional status field, interruptPending; the Deployment gains optional PPROF_PORT and GOMEMLIMIT_FRACTION env; the manager Role narrows Secret access to the webhook serving-cert Secret by name and drops pods/log; values move the operator image to v0.21.0, keep the v7.0.0 agent, and gain a values schema for runtimeRequiredTaint. The KWOK Tier 1 and Tier 2 lanes on the pull request for NVIDIA/aicr#3694 installed v0.21.0. Upstream release note operator/v0.21.0 for the behavior changes."
components.summary: Drain now evicts kube-system pods like any other namespace instead of skipping them, so CoreDNS and similar workloads are evicted before an interrupt rather than killed by the reboot. Eviction honors any PodDisruptionBudget that covers a pod; a workload with no budget can lose every replica on the nodes drained together. A kube-system PodDisruptionBudget that allows no disruptions holds the drain until spec.drainConfig.timeout, which AICR's tuning CRs leave unset, and with the default drainConfig an evicted pod's emptyDir data is deleted and a pod with no controller is not recreated. The operator also stops writing the last-logs Job annotation. Nothing to change on upgrade; before upgrading, confirm kubectl get pdb -n kube-system shows ALLOWED DISRUPTIONS of at least 1 for workloads on nodes NodeWright interrupts.

components.explanation: recorded manual: the record covering 1.31.0 describes the move from v1.28.0 to v1.31.0. Follow the steps below, then apply
components.summary: Three changes need operator action. A fatal health-events-analyzer event now cordons and drains its node through a new default fault-quarantine rule set, where v1.28.0 set only a node condition; it applies when the analyzer's effective processingStrategy is EXECUTE_REMEDIATION. With the remediation step and R610 or later drivers, XID 154 recovery actions now reset the GPU or reboot the node, where v1.28.0 reported CONTACT_SUPPORT. A custom generic-provider rebootImage without sh and cat no longer reboots nodes.
components.precondition: Where health-events-analyzer is deployed, its module-level processingStrategy and the processing_strategy of every enabled rule are neither EXECUTE_REMEDIATION nor UNSPECIFIED (an absent module value is the chart default, EXECUTE_REMEDIATION, and platform-connectors converts UNSPECIFIED to it), or fault-quarantine.ruleSets is set without the "Health events analyzer fatal error ruleset", or you accept that fatal analyzer events cordon and drain nodes from v1.31.0. Where the remediation step is composed and nodes run R610 or later drivers, you accept that an XID 154 recovery action resets the GPU or reboots the node, or you keep syslog-health-monitor events out of remediation. Where janitor-provider.csp.generic.rebootImage is a custom image, it contains sh and cat.

steps.description: Where health-events-analyzer is deployed, read the effective strategies from the nv-sentinel values in the bundle: the module-level processingStrategy, and the processing_strategy of each enabled rule in health-events-analyzer.config, which replaces the module value for that rule when it is set. An absent module value is the chart default, EXECUTE_REMEDIATION, not STORE_ONLY: only the nvsentinel-health-events-analyzer mixin sets STORE_ONLY. UNSPECIFIED counts as EXECUTE_REMEDIATION too, because platform-connectors converts it. Also read fault-quarantine.ruleSets: when set, it replaces the chart's list, and the v1.31.0 rule set that cordons for a fatal analyzer event applies only while the effective list still contains "Health events analyzer fatal error ruleset". If a strategy above is EXECUTE_REMEDIATION and that rule set is present, a fatal analyzer event cordons and drains its node: accept that, or keep the v1.28.0 condition-only behavior by setting fault-quarantine.ruleSets to the chart's v1.31.0 default list without that rule set (carry every other rule set, since the list replaces the default). Setting STORE_ONLY instead also removes the node condition and the Kubernetes Event that EXECUTE_REMEDIATION set, so alerts that read them stop; set it at the module level and change or remove every enabled rule's own processing_strategy: EXECUTE_REMEDIATION, because a rule that keeps it still cordons and drains.
steps.reason: The new default rule set cordons for a fatal analyzer event, and fault-quarantine reads only EXECUTE_REMEDIATION events, so that strategy, set or inherited, is what turns a condition-only signal into a drain.

steps.description: Where the nvsentinel-remediation step is composed and any node runs an R610 or later driver, expect an XID 154 recovery action (PF FLR, OS Reboot, Bus Reset or System Reboot) to reset that GPU or reboot the node, where v1.28.0 cordoned and drained the node for the fatal event and repaired nothing. No setting restores that: the monitor's action mapping has no per-XID switch. To stop syslog events from acting at all, regenerate the bundle with --set nv-sentinel:syslog-health-monitor.processingStrategy=STORE_ONLY, which also stops their cordon and drain and keeps them from the analyzer's rules, since STORE_ONLY events are not analyzer input, and read the processingStrategy of each NIC pattern in the monitor's config, because a pattern's own value replaces the module's.
steps.reason: v1.31.0 maps the R610 wordings to COMPONENT_RESET and RESTART_BM, which fault-remediation acts on; v1.28.0 mapped them to CONTACT_SUPPORT, which it does not.

steps.description: Where the nvsentinel-remediation step is composed with janitor-provider.csp.provider: generic, read janitor-provider.csp.generic.rebootImage in the bundle. The shipped BusyBox image is compatible. A custom image must contain sh and cat: the v1.31.0 reboot Job first reads the host boot ID with cat and refuses to reboot when it cannot, which v1.28.0 did not do. Check the image with kubectl run reboot-image-check --rm -i --restart=Never --image=<image> -- sh -c 'cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id'.
steps.reason: A reboot image without cat makes every reboot Job exit non-zero before it reboots, so RESTART_VM and RESTART_BM repairs never reboot the node.

steps.description: Re-run install.sh (helm), or commit the regenerated bundle and reconcile or sync it (flux, argocd, argocd-helm).
steps.reason: These deployers apply the chart's CRDs themselves, then roll the DaemonSets and Deployments to v1.31.0.
